text:
Alex: quick heads-up — after the runtime change that landed yesterday (commit fa1b2c3) we're seeing a ~12-18% p50 regression for medium-length sequences (seq=512) on the A100 pool.
Priya: ack. do we have nsys traces from before/after? rough hotspots?
Alex: yes. i captured two short nsys captures: before=nsys_before.qdrep, after=nsys_after.qdrep. timeline shows more time in kernel_selector and memcpy on the after-run.
Jamie: can you paste the nvprof/nsys cmd you used? i want to reproduce locally.
Alex: run i used:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,kernel --output=after --sample=none \ 
  --force-overwrite --stats true \ 
  --capture-range=none --duration=30s -- python3 run_inference.py --model gpt-medium --seq 512
```
Connor: i compared flamegraphs quickly — the after trace moves ~25% of time from fused_attention kernel to a small fallback attention kernel (attention_fallback()) + a lot more small memcopies for KV stitching.
Priya: that sounds like kernel selection picked a non-optimal variant. did the selector heuristic change? i remember a recent PR that prefers 2D tiled kernels when batch<4.
Alex: yes PR #2384 tweaked heuristics (favor tiled2D for lower batch sizes) — i suspect the heuristic now misclassifies our medium sequences. see snippet from selector log in the after trace:
```
[selector] seq=512 batch=2 estimated_warp=28 -> chosen_kernel=tiled2D_v2 (score=0.42)
[selector] seq=512 batch=2 fallback_kernel=attention_fused (score=0.40)
```
Jamie: interesting — score delta is tiny. slight upstream timing noise could flip it. can you diff the kernel timelines? any change in launch latency or occupancy?
Alex: diff shows tiled2D_v2 has ~8ms higher lifetime per token (due to extra memcopies) even though core compute is slightly faster. overall adds ~14% to p50.
perf-bot: automatic bisect kicked off (range: fa1b2c3..e9d8c7a). current suspect commit: 7b1c9f2 — kernel-selector thresholds adjusted.
Connor: i ran an nvprof sample focusing on memcopies; here's the condensed output after:
```
== API Calls ==
Memcpy HtoD : 120 calls, total 4.6s
Memcpy DtoH : 3 calls, total 0.02s
Kernel tiled2D_v2 : 340 calls, total 6.1s
Kernel attention_fused : 240 calls, total 4.7s
```
Priya: those extra HtoD calls are the killer. tiled2D_v2 is forcing host staging for kv pages in our path.
Jamie: plan: 1) bisect to confirm commit 7b1c9f2 is the regression. 2) add a safety threshold so if score delta < 0.05 prefer the previously stable fused kernel. 3) add a KV cache-prefetch affinity flag so tiled kernels don't trigger host staging.
Alex: bisect result: CONFIRMED — 7b1c9f2 introduced change. i pushed a quick revert/guard branch (hotfix/kselector-safety) that restores old tie-break behavior.
Connor: after hotfix run, p50 returned to baseline in our small cluster tests. attached perfetto link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/ui?url=toytrace (mock)
Priya: nice. can you add a unit/regression test that exercises seq=512 batch=2 hotpath and validates kernel choice + no extra HtoD memcpys? also add an nsight timeline artifact to the PR so QE can eyeball.
Alex: on it. i'll open PR with the guard + test + traces. PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2401
Jamie: also flag this for dedicated infra: some customers pin batch sizes that will hit this. we should include a rollout note and monitor token-level latency for 24h after deploy.
perf-bot: alert rule created: monitor.eng-runtime.kselector.p50_increase if p50 increases >8% for seq in [256,512,1024] for 30m.
Alex: thanks all. i'll keep this thread updated with PR merges and CI runs. :thumbsup:
Connor: thanks — great bisect work. :eyes:
Priya: nice detective work. once merged, let's schedule a perf-run across the A100/FSDP fleet.
Jamie: added a short checklist to the PR for post-merge validation.
Alex: last note — saving the nsys captures in s3://redwood-perf/collections/2026-03-18/kselector-regression/{before,after,hotfix}.qdrep for reference.
